papers.title: A generalised and modular proof-theoretic semantics for sequent systems
papers.abstract: Base-extension semantics explains logical consequence via derivability in atomic systems. Extending this approach across logics requires careful control of structural principles and contexts. We present a modular sequent-based framework in which support is indexed by multisets of atomic resources and the semantic clauses for connectives are guided by their left introduction rules. The framework separates additive from multiplicative behaviour and makes explicit the contributions of structural rules and restrictions on sequents. We establish soundness and completeness for classical and intuitionistic propositional logic and for multiplicative-additive fragments of classical and intuitionistic linear logic. We then investigate axiomatic extensions of intuitionistic logic through Jankov logic. Two classes of atomic bases yield sound and complete semantics. Completeness is proven using two novel and modular methods using simulation bases, one of which is constructive. These results provide a common semantic treatment of several logical systems while identifying the additional conditions needed to extend the framework beyond structural variations.

papers.title: Model completeness for the differential field of transseries with exponentiation
papers.abstract: We show that the expansion of the valued differential field of logarithmic-exponential transseries by its natural exponential function is model complete. We give an axiomatization of the theory of this expansion that is effective relative to the theory of the real exponential field, and show that any maximal Hardy field satisfies the same axioms. We use this to prove a transfer theorem between Hardy fields and transseries.

papers.title: The Compactness Theorem for Enriched Logic
papers.abstract: The framework of enriched logic extends positive logic (also known as coherent logic) from sets to structures internal to a symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal{V}$. This framework was developed by Rosick\'y and the second-named author. The main novelty of this logic is that the arities of the function and relation symbols are now objects in $\mathcal{V}$. We prove the compactness theorem for this enriched logic. That is, a set of $\mathcal{V}$-enriched sequents has a model (internal to $\mathcal{V}$) if every finite subset has a model. To achieve this, we define ultraproducts of enriched structures and prove enriched versions of {\L}os' theorem. We then develop some model-theoretic applications. We start with an enriched version of the model-theoretic method of diagrams, establishing a correspondence between homomorphisms whose domain is some enriched structure $A$ and models of the set $\operatorname{Diag}(A)$ of all enriched atomic formulas with parameters from $A$ that are true in $A$. Combining this with our compactness theorem, we prove amalgamation results, laying the foundations for enriched syntactic types (in the model-theoretic sense). We finish the paper with a collection of examples of $\mathcal{V}$ that our results apply to. Besides recovering the classical case when $\mathcal{V} = \mathbf{Set}$, these include many presheaf toposes, categories of monoid acts, the category of abelian groups and related additive categories, categories of (small) enriched categories, and the categories of posets and pseudometric spaces.

papers.title: A Zero--One Law for Subrings of the Reals Closed under Binary Interleaving
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s Problem 1154 asks whether every number in $[0,1]$ occurs as the Hausdorff dimension of a subring or subfield of $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that a subring of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under binary interleaving has Hausdorff dimension either zero or one. Consequently, every Turing ideal and its associated subfield satisfy the same dichotomy.

papers.title: Finite index extensions of treeable equivalence relations are treeable
papers.abstract: We prove that every countable Borel equivalence relation containing a finite index Borel treeable subequivalence relation is Borel treeable. This answers a long-standing question of Jackson--Kechris--Louveau. Our proof is based on a median subalgebra filtration construction on products of trees, together with an extension of the median graph treeing algorithm of Chen--Poulin--Tao--Tserunyan to certain well-behaved increasing unions.

papers.title: Proof Perplexity: A Probabilistic Approach to Measuring non-triviality in Machine Generated Proofs
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose a benchmark to quantify the non-triviality and novelty of machine-generated mathematical proofs compared to existing literature. Our core methodology uses a probabilistic measure to evaluate the non-triviality of the underlying mathematical arguments in comparison to the current \texttt{MATHLIB} library. Finally, we apply this benchmark to the recent proof generated by Claude on the complex zeros of the Riemann zeta function to test for non-trivial steps.

papers.title: Models of Arbitrary Sets
papers.abstract: There is a growing literature on arbitrary objects as other types of mathematical objects, besides particular mathematical objects. In this paper we study arbitrary sets in the context of ZFC set theory. An arbitrary object is one that is determined by a state space across which it varies and by its instantiations. We compare two semantic strategies. First, we analyse the possibility of modeling arbitrary sets using direct powers of a ZFC structure. This yields a natural setting, but one where Extensionality and, crucially, the full Separation scheme fail. Second, we consider structures composed of arbitrary sets using a direct power construction evaluated in a Boolean-valued semantics. Within this setting, we develop the cumulative hierarchy of arbitrary sets, arbitrary ordinals, cardinals, and filtrations of the structure of arbitrary sets. The final section develops a combinatorial interpretation in terms of independent assignments across a fixed state space. Its connection with the iterative conception is then discussed.

papers.title: A technical note on universal formula pcas
papers.abstract: We record some interesting technical caveats found when using universal formulae to formulate pcas -- namely, that there are different ways to extract a (partial) function from a definable collection of pairs, and these choices have an impact on formula complexity.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables I: stable and uniformly stable observables
papers.abstract: When two quantum systems are prepared independently and each is driven to an idealized limit, the expectation of a bipartite observable may depend on which system is idealized first. We call an observable stable when it does not. We show that stability is equivalent to two operational properties. First, every idealized preparation of one system can be simulated to arbitrary accuracy, uniformly over all probes, by finite mixtures of actual preparations, provided that the probing system is idealized first. Second, any two idealized preparations have a unique, symmetric independent product. Under a uniform form of stability, we prove, the number of preparations that $n$ adaptive probes can tell apart at a fixed margin is bounded by a polynomial in $n$, and responses can be learned with a bounded number of mistakes; otherwise, at some margin, protocols with $n$ probes tell apart $2^n$ preparations. The swap test, Hong--Ou--Mandel coincidences and discrete equality tests turn out to be uniformly stable, with bounds independent of the dimension, while order comparisons of discrete spectra unbounded above are unstable. The proofs rest on the classical fact that a single double limit condition appears, under different names, in topology (Grothendieck), functional analysis (Krivine--Maurey), algebra (Arens), probability (Simons) and combinatorics (Pt\'ak), and in model theory as Shelah's stability, where the independent product corresponds to Harrington's lemma. Model theory thus serves as a Rosetta stone, pairing each physical question with its mathematical formulation.

papers.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
papers.abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.

papers.title: Schnorr Randomness and Effective Bayesian Consistency and Inconsistency
papers.abstract: We study Doob's Consistency Theorem and Freedman's Inconsistency Theorem from the vantage point of computable probability and algorithmic randomness. We show that the Schnorr random elements of the parameter space are computably consistent, when there is a map from the sample space to the parameter space satisfying many of the same properties as limiting relative frequencies. We show that the generic inconsistency in Freedman's Theorem is effectively comeager, which implies the existence of computable parameters which are not computably consistent. Taken together, this work provides a computability-theoretic solution to Diaconis and Freedman's problem of ``know[ing] for which [parameters] the rule [Bayes' rule] is consistent'', and it strengthens recent similar results of Takahashi on Martin-L\"of randomness in Cantor space.

papers.title: Herbrand Game Complexity
papers.abstract: The Student-Teacher game is an extension of Herbrand's theorem. In the game, Student and Teacher take turns giving values for existentially and universally quantified variables, and Student is allowed to backtrack to propose other values for existentially quantified variables. The game has become increasingly important for proving lower bounds on provability in theories of bounded arithmetic. In those applications, the game is played in an arithmetical theory; however, this paper studies the Student-Teacher game in the setting of pure first-order logic, so it is more closely related to Herbrand's theorem and the midsequent theorem. When played in pure first-order logic, a prenex formula $\phi$ is logically valid if and only if there is a Student-Teacher game with a winning strategy for Student for establishing $\phi$. We present a refined version of the Student-Teacher game in arbitrary first-order universal theories and include a proof of the validity of Student-Teacher games from the sequent calculus midsequent theorem in an appendix. The game is presented as a finite tree with vertices and edges labeled by terms, and with a total order on the nodes. The totally ordered tree represents the players' interaction. Our main results show that minimal trees in the Student-Teacher game can be arbitrarily complex. Specifically, for every totally ordered tree $T$, we construct a valid prenex formula $\phi$ such that every winning Student-Teacher game for $\phi$ contains $T$ as a substructure. Using formulas parameterized by numerals, we prove similar results for computable and partial computable sequences of totally ordered trees. It follows not only that there is no computable bound on the size of Herbrand disjunctions, which is a well-known fact, but also that there is no computable bound on their complexity.

papers.title: There is no maximal $K$-degree
papers.abstract: The Kolmogorov complexity of a string characterize how complex it is to describe the string. If every prefix of a real $x$ is more complex to describe than every prefix (of the same length) of real $y$, then it is seen as $x$ is more complex to describe than $y$. It is wondered if there is a real $x$ so that no other reals are strictly more complex (to describe) than $x$. The behavior of Kolmogorov complexity functions generated by reals (namely $n\mapsto$ the minimal description length of the real) is quite chaos. Therefore, it is widely believed that there are many reals that are maximally complex to describe. For instance, it is conjectured that all random enough reals have maximal $K$-degree. In this paper, it is shown that there is no real with maximal $K$-degree. Actually, for almost all real $x$, we can uniformly computably find another real whose $K$-degree is strictly above $x$. The same construction also derives the following: (a) There is no maximal $C $-degree. (b) Every $n$-random real $x$ admits an $n$-random real $y$ such that $y>_Kx$ and $y>_C x$; moreover, the difference of $K$-complexity and $C$-complexity of $y,x$ (namely $K(y\upharpoonright n)-K(x\upharpoonright n)$ and $C(y\upharpoonright n)-C(x\upharpoonright n)$) do not tend to infinity.

papers.title: What David Teaches Goliath: An Inevitable Extension of ZFC
papers.abstract: We examine the metamathematical significance of the Levy scheme $\Lambda$, which asserts, for each natural number $n$, the existence of an $n$-Mahlo cardinal $\kappa$ such that $V_\kappa\prec_{\Sigma_n}V$. Several initially unrelated constructions single out $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$: comparisons with the model theory of arithmetic and finite set theory; class theories in which the class of ordinals has the tree property; set theories with a proper class of indiscernibles; and interpretations of ordinary set theory in Cantorian parts of models of the extension \mathsf{NFUA} of Quine--Jensen set theory $\mathsf{NFU}$. Taken together, the results surveyed here provide a precise sense in which $\mathsf{ZFC}+\Lambda$ is an inevitable extension of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ if one attempts to generalize certain metamathematical results about the microcosm of hereditarily finite sets to the entire macrocosm of sets.

papers.title: Indiscernible Extraction in Theories with Bounded $k$-splitting
papers.abstract: Hanson introduced the class of theories with bounded $k$-splitting, a higher-arity notion of stability, and proved an indiscernible extraction result for those theories assuming the existence of a $k$-ineffable cardinal. In this article, we show that the conclusion of Hanson's theorem is equivalent to the weaker assertion that there exists a weakly compact cardinal, as well as prove additional indiscernible extraction results for these theories in ZFC. Finally, we show that Hanson's construction of total bounded ultraimaginary Morley sequences in theories with bounded $k$-splitting follows from ZFC.
